title: PDE-PFN: Prior-Data Fitted Neural PDE Solver
claim: A transformer pre-trained on noisy approximate data infers solutions from observed context in-context, with no gradient updates at inference.
layout: 3 regions, left-to-right; green inference box with feedback loop arrow
description: A left-to-right workflow diagram. At left, a light-blue panel titled 'Noisy Prior Data' holds a 2x2 grid of heatmaps: the top two are heavily speckled and the bottom two are fainter. A 'Pre-train' arrow leads to a green box titled 'Zero-gradient Update for Parameters'. Inside it, a gray 'Transformer for In-Context Learning' block states that it infers the solution at queries given the observations. An 'Input' arrow runs from a legend box ('Observed Data (or Context)' shown as a color gradient swatch, 'Queries' shown as an open circle). That box is fed by a sparse scatter-point field at far right. An 'Output' arrow leads to a smooth, clean viridis solution heatmap. A dotted curved arrow labeled 'Solution' returns from the heatmap to the scatter field. The caption 'Visible region to the model during inference' sits at the bottom of the green box.
caption: The overall workflow of PDE-PFN. Our model performs in-context learning (ICL) based on given observations (i.e., context) to infer solutions. At inference, PDE-PFN conditions on observations from the target instance without separate operator-level demonstrations or target-instance gradient updates. Even when trained with an approximated PINN prior, our method can improve over noisy approximate pretraining data.
abstract: Motivated by the success of large language models (LLMs) with broad generalizability and robustness to noisy or unreliable pre-training data, we explore in-context prediction of PDE solution fields using approximate pre-training data. In addition, inspired by the posterior predictive mean-based inference mechanism of the in-context learning in prior-data fitted networks (PFNs), we propose PDE-PFN, a prior-data fitted neural solver that approximates the posterior predictive mean of PDE solutions via in-context learning. PDE-PFN builds on a PFN architecture with self- and cross-attention mechanisms of Transformer and is pre-trained on noisy approximate solutions generated by physics-informed neural networks, serving as diverse but not necessarily exact priors. Through experiments on a range of two-dimensional PDEs, we demonstrate that PDE-PFN achieves empirical generalization across heterogeneous equations, robustness under noisy priors, and zero-gradient-update in-context inference capability. PDE-PFN achieves competitive or improved predictive accuracy relative to the evaluated baselines while supporting flexible context and query representations.
